mainEntity.name: How much does a gallon of paint cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Manufacturers usually state 350 to 400 square feet per gallon on smooth, primed walls. Textured, porous or unprimed surfaces soak up more paint and can drop coverage to 250 to 300 square feet per gallon.
Use primer on new drywall, bare wood, patched areas, stains, and when moving from a glossy or oil-based paint to latex. A good paint-and-primer can replace it on already-painted, clean walls.
Two coats give a durable, even finish for most jobs. One coat can work for touch-ups in the same colour, and three may be needed for a big colour change such as dark to light.

mainEntity.name: How do I measure a vaulted ceiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a sloped ceiling, find the sloped length with the Pythagorean theorem (√(rise² + run²)) and multiply by the room length. Add the triangular gable wall, which is ½ × base × height.

mainEntity.name: How should I store leftover paint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seal the lid tightly, store the can upside down or on its side if the manufacturer allows, and keep it somewhere cool and dry above freezing. Label it with the colour, room and date.
